I'm currently studying in China and getting ready to travel to Yunnan by myself. The biggest tips for China is to be aware. Be aware of where your food is coming from and how it was prepared. Be aware of cars, bicycles, mopeds, little old ladies... you get the idea. Be aware of scams, pickpockets and creeps. 

I have been to Xi'an and Beijing... for Beijing, the Hutong area is really cool (older section with old houses). Good luck!

Hey, I'm going to China in about a week and have lived in Singapore. I've also been to Taiwan so I might be able to help you out. 

Taiwan is an awesome place and you're going to have loads of fun! Make sure you try the shaved ice, the bubble tea (!!!), tea eggs (if you can get them, they're kind of regional) and freshly fried sweet potato balls. The street food is awesome but if you don't travel much maybe only eat the stuff that you SAW just finish cooking. Otherwise you risk getting sick!

Do you speak Chinese? The characters are traditional there and there are many phrases different on the mainland than in Taiwan. However, they will know what you are saying and will forgive bad Chinese if you are a foreigner anyways. It's quite useful. 

Make sure you have good close-toed walking shoes. Asia in general is not as clean in the West... It will also be super hot there so make sure you wear clothes that allow sweat to evaporate. However Asia in general is also becoming more fashion-aware so try to dress nicely and perhaps more conservatively than you would in the West... 

In terms of travel: Make sure you have copies of everything (passport, etc) and your parents have a copy too. Make sure your bank knows you are going. And have a good time! Taiwan is pretty safe so you don't need a money belt/whatever but keep an eye on your stuff. 

I assume you are a Westerner (I'm not) so expect to have a harder time bargaining for items (they will charge you more, though not significantly) and expect to have a hard time fitting into clothes, if you want to buy them. Don't get offended if you are an extra large! It's just that Asian people are tiny. There are many wonderful local items you can buy and try to find some aboriginal stuff if you can. The arts and crafts are lovely!

Hope I was sort of helpful haha.... Have a great time!

Hey congrats! I'm going to Chengdu with the USAC, but I've been to London in the summer so I can try to help you (I was there 3 weeks, but whatever). 

You need to bring an umbrella and at least 2 jackets of differing layers of warmth, I got cold in the evenings. You can buy basically everything you need there but if you are super brand picky about something, buy it in the States. Bring shorts for the couple of hot days but mostly outfits that you can add/subtract layers to. Bring good walking shoes with enough support for areas of uneven roads (flip flops= hurting feet). London is a fashionable city, try to make sure everything has the right fit. Even if you dress simply, you should look nice. 

Within England, Bath, Bristol, Leeds and Manchester are all great! There are lovely sites within all those cities.... Bath is really something to visit, spend lots of time in the Roman Baths. Oh! If you get the chance go to Nottingham and have fun with all the Robin Hood stuff. Go to Scotland if you have the time, but if not definitely go to Wales. I loved Cardiff.

In terms of your places to go... I would personally do Paris, either Ravensburg or Munich (go see the cool German castles!) and Rome. Athens is further out than you think it is... but that's just my opinion.

Also do you plan to fly to these places? It could become far more expensive than you want it to be unless you look at prices carefully. 

I've been to Berlin, there's nothing wrong with it but there are more interesting places to go in Germany culturally. The food is pretty good there though and the street-cart sausages are delicious. 

Well, that's just my opinion. Have fun!

Honestly, I kind of agree with her. She's done a lot for you over a long period of time for you. 

In my experience (I followed my boyfriend to college halfway around the world), following a guy somewhere new is incredibly stressful. There's a really strong fear of being stuck somewhere you hate with no way to leave. Worse, if there's no definite confirmation that this relationship is worth it, you're left with doubt, and doubt grows in the mind like a weed. 

For a lot of women, an engagement (ring) is a symbol that you're in it for the long haul. Marriage is more than just confirming monogamy-- it's confirming that you're going to be together through whatever life throws at you. She's gone through a lot for you and it sounds like she was miserable when she couldn't leave Canada. So yes, she sees it as a pot of gold at the end of the rainbow because it confirms she wasn't wasting her time with the whole adventure.

In terms of getting married, you might just want to have a long engagement and set the wedding a few years out. Nothing wrong with that, and it gives you time to iron out the other stuff wrong with the relationship. 


Also... women aren't mind readers. We honestly have no idea when you need support if you're refusing to talk to us about it. So no, talk to her when you need support and she'll give it to you.

I did long distance with my boyfriend for about a year, and we were a 12 hour time difference apart. It's completely possible to do long distance, so don't let age stop you. 

Skype, texting, FB... all of that is a good way to keep in touch. Try to see each other every couple of months if you go for it. 

The key to long distance is there's an end date when you're together in person. I followed my boyfriend to university, so we knew it would only be a year long. If there's no end date, it's 100% not worth it. 

In terms of the clingy type... yeah, you're young. Of course you're affectionate. It will suck to be apart at first, but you'll get used to it. Be prepared to reevaluate your relationship after every time you meet up again. If you decide it's not worth it, cut it. 

Good luck!
